lesson.menu_desc: Reading the numbers of a small fintech and asking about money and quantities -- how much / how many
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- Numbers Behind the Card
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ender de Souza Batista | Lesson 10 -- Numbers Behind the Card
lesson.grammar_point: how much (uncountable: money, time) / how many (countable: clients, transactions) + big numbers (thousand, million)

listenings.text: Okay, everyone, the numbers of the month. How many new stores are in the program? Two hundred. Great work. How many cards? Three million. How many problems? Only five, and they are small. How much money is it? A lot, and the report has every number. The next call is short: only thirty minutes. Thank you!

My bank is big. How many cards? About ten million. But in India, many payments are very small. How much is a cup of tea at a small shop? About twenty rupees. People pay for that with the phone! So how many transactions are there in a day? A lot: about two million. Every transaction is small, but every transaction is important.

extra_audio.text: Nova Pay is a small fintech in São Paulo. There are about fifty thousand clients. There are about one million transactions in a month. The store pays a fee of two percent. Every Monday, the director reads the report.

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: one payment, from the card to the store

paras: Nova Pay is a small fintech in São Paulo. How many clients are there? About fifty thousand. How many stores use Nova Pay? Two thousand. And every month, there are about one million transactions.

How much money is in one transaction? Usually not much. The price of a coffee is about ten reais, and a lunch is about forty. The store pays a small fee for every payment: two percent. Small payments, but many of them!

Every Monday, the director reads the report. How many transactions? How much money? How many problems? This week, there are not many problems: only three. And how much coffee does the team drink? A lot!
